earlier_development_boundary.observation: List comprehension exposed only first raised future; other raw worker evidence generally remained but later exceptions before launch were not aggregated. Author independently found same gap. New collector addresses this scope.

limits: Static scheduling/identity/merge review only; does not prove compiler correctness or successful final native qualification
Outer deadline, subreaper ownership and descendant cleanup are a separate ABI peer review and actual controlled execution gate
A disk failure can prevent receipt persistence; such failure rejects qualification, and this review does not claim complete evidence despite failed storage
No claim of cross-file transactional snapshots, full language support, runtime attestation, NDU economic benefit, or production cutover
scope: B0 and original/mutated three-generation native chains remain sequential before family scheduling
20 exact family/compiler-label pairs with maximum two host-oracle workers, fresh -I -S -B Python process and unique phase directory per pair
Compiler/source/sample/mutation/reference input hashes plus source-manifest before/after bind each worker; ELF sample uses current fresh chain bytes, not historical seed
Parent verifies worker PID, family/label, complete expected input hashes, interpreter flags, source manifest and process identity
Merge requires complete unique closed inventory, nonempty strict-bool checks, status consistent with checks and no check overwrite; false results remain false

All scheduled futures are now consumed through as_completed; successful and exceptional outcomes, including before-Popen errors, remain in the atomic phase index; ordinary errors prevent aggregate PASS and control exceptions are rethrown after observation
Existing native invoke still starts a distinct child; added -S disables site loading without process reuse
